::: {#lem-level-parent}
#### A child is one level below its parent

Let $v$ be a vertex of a rooted tree (@def-rooted-tree) other than the root $r$, and let $u$ be its parent (@def-tree-parent).
Then the path from $r$ to $v$ is the path from $r$ to $u$ followed by $v$, and

$$
\operatorname{level}(v) = \operatorname{level}(u) + 1.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Let $r = v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_k = v$ be the path from $r$ to $v$, so that $u = v_{k - 1}$.
The vertices $v_0, \ldots, v_{k - 1}$ are all different,
so $v_0, \ldots, v_{k - 1}$ is a path from $r$ to $u$,
and by @thm-tree-paths it is the path from $r$ to $u$.
Its length is $k - 1$, so $\operatorname{level}(u) = k - 1 = \operatorname{level}(v) - 1$ (@def-tree-level).

:::

:::
